title: Quantization latency budgeter and adaptive dequant routing for prefill/decode
creator: Anika Rao
description: Problem: Dequantization overhead and mixed-precision handoffs are a measurable contributor to tail latency during prefill and decode, especially for multimodel routing where requests can move between INT8, FP8 and FP16 variants. This ticket proposes an adaptive dequant routing layer that budgets dequant time per-request and dynamically chooses a kernel/precision handoff strategy to meet per-request latency SLOs while preserving end-to-end quality. Goals: 1) reduce p95/p99 latency regressions caused by synchronous dequant steps, 2) provide a deterministic microbudget for dequant work inside the serving runtime, 3) integrate with kernel selector to prefer zero-copy or amortized dequant kernels when beneficial, 4) expose telemetry to show quality vs cost vs latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: New adaptive dequant router integrated into serving runtime that picks one of: zero-copy passthrough, amortized batched dequant, async background dequant with KV cache continuation, or full sync dequant fallback.
Demonstrated p95 latency improvement >= 12% on internal prefill-heavy workload (long-context chat synthetic trace) versus baseline runtime-2.3 with same models quantized to INT8/FP8.
End-to-end token quality delta (perplexity / BLEU proxy on eval set) within 0.5% for chosen fallback thresholds, and documented config knobs to trade quality for latency.
Telemetry dashboard with per-request chosen dequant strategy, dequant time budget consumed, and kernel selection reason.
Automated unit + integration tests covering kernel selection heuristics and fallback correctness.
tasks: Design: define per-request latency budget model and thresholds for dequant strategies (Anika)
Implement dequant routing API and strategy registry in runtime (Mateo)
Add kernel hints for zero-copy and amortized dequant kernels to kernel selector (runtime team)
Implement async background dequant path that resumes KV-prefill when dequant completes (prefill team)
Bench: run synthetic prefill/decode traces across INT8/FP8/FP16 variants and capture p50/p95/p99 (Bench team)
Add telemetry hooks and console dashboard tiles (observability)
PR: code review, perf review, and merge (all)
notes: 2026-02-20: Initial intake — observed repeated p99 spikes on long-context multi-batch decode where dequant dominated wall time. Logged traces and flamegraphs point to synchronous epilogue pipelines.

2026-02-24: Discussion with kernel team: several kernels support 'zero-copy dequant' by operating on packed int buffers and emitting FP outputs into downstream accumulators; need explicit hinting from selector to prefer those when latency budget tight.

2026-03-02: Prototype: async-dequant branch that offloads dequant to background worker and continues KV-prefill showed 9% p95 improvement on 8k-context synthetic workload but small quality regressions for edge-case quant scales. Saved prototype at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428

2026-03-05: Design decision: use per-request soft budget computed as max(global_budget * request_length_scale, min_budget). If strategy completes before budget, continue sync path; if overrun, switch to fallback sync dequant to preserve correctness. Added config knobs for tuning in canary.

2026-03-07: PM review (Jordan Lee): asked for explicit audit trail in logs for any request that switched strategy mid-flight and flagged as potential debugging export to S3. Added acceptance criteria accordingly.

2026-03-09: Security review note: non-sensitive, but ensure background workers respect tenant isolation and zero-copy paths don't expose upstream buffer contents across tenants. Security signoff scheduled as part of runtime-2.4 gating.

2026-03-10: Performance benchmarks: end-to-end p95 improved 14% on internal chat trace with INT8 models when using adaptive routing + amortized kernels; CPU overhead of router negligible (<1% request CPU). Collected artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/runtime/quant-budgeter/benchmark-2026-03-10.csv
risks: Quality regression if quant scales differ across layers and amortized dequant approximations propagate error; mitigate with per-layer validation samples and conservative canary thresholds.
Increased complexity in kernel selector heuristics could cause suboptimal choices under cold-start; mitigated by defaulting to safe sync path until telemetry warms up.
Cross-tenant memory safety for zero-copy requires careful buffer lifetime management; will add additional sanitizer tests in CI.
review_feedback: 2026-03-03 (Sreya K.): Prefer exposing budget knobs as sampling-based feature flags for canary to avoid global config churn.
2026-03-06 (Tomas H.): Please add an integration test that simulates sudden switch from INT8 to FP16 fallback and verifies KV cache continuity.
2026-03-08 (Priya N.): Add a console visualization showing how often amortized vs zero-copy strategies are used per model to help product conversations.
